chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Yahya, from Hariz, from Mu'alla ibn Khunays, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Mu'alla! Conceal our matter and do not broadcast it, for whoever conceals our matter and does not broadcast it, Allah will honor him because of it in the world, and make it a light between his eyes in the Hereafter, guiding him to Paradise.'

O Mu'alla! Whoever broadcasts our matter and does not conceal it, Allah will humble him because of it in the world, and remove the light from between his eyes in the Hereafter, and make it a darkness guiding him to the Fire.
O Mu'alla! Indeed, dissimulation (Taqiyyah) is from my religion and the religion of my forefathers, and there is no religion for the one who has no dissimulation.
O Mu'alla! Indeed, Allah loves to be worshipped in secret just as He loves to be worshipped openly.
O Mu'alla! Indeed, the broadcaster of our matter is like the one who denies it.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّة: Dissimulation; the practice of concealing one's faith or beliefs in times of danger or oppression.
key_terms.الظُّلْمَة: Darkness; symbolizing misguidance and spiritual loss.
key_terms.النُّور: Light; symbolizing guidance and spiritual clarity.
key_terms.يُذِعْهُ: To broadcast or make public; to many people.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Taqiyyah (dissimulation) in Shia Islam according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the strategic necessity of Taqiyyah (dissimulation) as a fundamental pillar of Shia identity, rooted in the Prophet's family's experience during periods of political persecution. By linking the concealment of divine authority to spiritual light and honor, it elevates secrecy from mere survival to a theological virtue, while equating public proclamation with denial reflects the context of distinguishing true adherents from the general populace. The emphasis on Allah's preference for both secret and open worship highlights the versatility of devotion, ensuring that the core message remains preserved even when external circumstances demand discretion.
